title: Single-nucleus multimodal spatial transcriptomics reveals spatial colocalization of neoantigen-expressing tumor cells and cognate T cells - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Nagler, Sud and Ghannam (Dana-Farber / Broad / Harvard, senior authors Catherine J. Wu, Fei Chen, Nir Hacohen) introduce Slide-GoTags, a droplet-based single-nucleus spatial transcriptomics method that combines targeted transcript genotyping, TCR sequencing and snRNA-seq from the same frozen tissue slice. It shows clonally expanded neoantigen-specific T cells physically colocalizing with tumor cells expressing their cognate neoantigen in mouse MC38 and human ccRCC tumors, distinguishes anti-PD1 from anti-CTLA4 spatial immune landscapes, and finds interferon-driven immunogenicity niches enriched in immunologically hot tumors. Note: the record's `text` is the abstract, figure legends, extended data captions and front/back matter — the main body is behind subscription.

insights.claim: Slide-GoTags is a droplet-based single-nucleus spatial transcriptomics method that integrates targeted transcript genotyping and T cell receptor sequencing with single-nucleus RNA sequencing from the same slice of frozen tissue, rather than requiring separate assays on separate sections.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Same-slice multimodality removes the section-registration error that has limited every prior spatial-plus-TCR workflow, which is the technical bar a commercial kit would need to clear.
insights.quote: a droplet-based single-nucleus spatial transcriptomics approach that characterizes neoantigen-specific immunity by integrating targeted transcript genotyping and T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing with single-nucleus RNA sequencing

insights.claim: The genotyping workflow combines the Nanoranger long-read pipeline with Slide-GoTags for variant detection and genotype assignment to individual nuclei, meaning single-nucleotide tumor mutations are called per-cell and mapped in space.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Per-nucleus variant calling is what turns spatial transcriptomics into a neoantigen assay — the differentiator versus generic spatial platforms.

insights.claim: The method operates on frozen tissue rather than fresh samples, which matters because it makes archived biobank specimens addressable for retrospective neoantigen-immunity mapping.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Frozen-compatible workflows unlock existing trial sample archives — a far larger near-term run rate than prospective collection.

insights.claim: The team synthesized its own barcoded beads in-house (contributions credited to G.J.M. and V.K.), indicating the reagent supply chain is not yet a commercial off-the-shelf product.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: In-house bead synthesis is a bottleneck to third-party adoption and a natural entry point for a reagent vendor to license the method.

insights.claim: Applied to mouse and human tumors, Slide-GoTags revealed colocalization of clonally expanded, neoantigen-specific T cells with the tumor cells expressing their cognate neoantigen — direct in situ evidence that antigen-specific killing is spatially organised rather than diffuse.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Spatial colocalization becomes a candidate surrogate endpoint for whether a neoantigen vaccine or TIL product actually engaged its target in tissue.
insights.quote: Application of Slide-GoTags to mouse and human tumors revealed colocalization of clonally expanded, neoantigen-specific T cells with tumor cells expressing their cognate neoantigen.

insights.claim: In human clear cell renal cell carcinoma the team tracked the NSUN5 p.Q18K mutation across four serial tumor sections, mapping NSUN5-mutant tumor nuclei against T cells bearing NSUN5-specific TCRs, other tumor-specific TCRs, and unrelated clonotypes.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A named human neoantigen–TCR pair resolved in space is the proof point that translates the mouse work into a clinical-grade assay claim.

insights.claim: Nearest-distance between NSUN5-mutant tumor cells and NSUN5-specific T cells correlated with a chemokine/chemokine-receptor module score, suggesting chemokine signalling is what physically recruits cognate T cells to mutant tumor cells.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If chemokine tone sets T cell proximity, chemokine-axis agonists become a rational combination partner for neoantigen therapies.

insights.claim: In the mouse MC38-SIINFEKL model, SIINFEKL-genotyped tumor cells and OT-I T cells expressing the matching CDR3 TRA/TRB sequences were resolved separately from non-OT-I T cells, providing a controlled ground truth for the colocalization claim.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A synthetic-antigen positive control is what makes the human observational result credible; its absence is the usual weakness of spatial papers.

insights.claim: Anti-PD1 and anti-CTLA4 blockade produced distinct spatial immune landscapes in mouse colorectal (MC38) tumors, meaning the two checkpoint classes differ in tissue architecture and not only in cell-frequency readouts.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Spatial divergence between PD-1 and CTLA-4 mechanisms supports combination rationale and gives a readout to differentiate me-too checkpoint assets.
insights.quote: We also identified distinct spatial immune landscapes shaped by anti-PD1 or anti-CTLA4 blockade in mouse colorectal tumors.

insights.claim: In anti-PD1-treated mice, T cells colocalized with antigen-presenting cancer-associated fibroblasts marked by dual CD74 and S100A4 expression, quantified by immunofluorescence across six mice per group and 36 images per mouse.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Implicates the stromal compartment as an active participant in PD-1 response — a target class (apCAFs) distinct from tumor or T cell directed drugs.

insights.claim: The mouse checkpoint experiment ran with a single untreated animal against three anti-CTLA-4 and three anti-PD-1 animals, so the treatment-landscape comparison rests on very small group sizes.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: n=1 control is the main statistical soft spot in the paper — treat the ICB-landscape claims as hypothesis-generating until replicated.

insights.claim: Six distinct MC38 neoantigens beyond the dominant Rpl18 p.Q125R — Adgpk9 p.R304M, Atg9a p.L299Q, Cpne1 p.L299Q, Tmem135 p.R421L, Dpagt1 p.V213L and Ndfip2 p.A238P — were genotyped and spatially mapped simultaneously, showing the assay is multiplexed across mutations rather than single-target.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Multiplexed neoantigen genotyping is what makes the assay usable for polyclonal vaccines, where single-epitope readouts are useless.

insights.claim: Across human tumor types, interferon-driven immunogenicity niches were enriched in immunologically hot tumors compared with cold tumors, and those niches harboured three T cell clonotypes that colocalized with genotyped neoantigens.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Gives the hot/cold tumor dichotomy a concrete spatial-molecular definition (interferon niche presence) that could be turned into a companion diagnostic.
insights.quote: Across human tumor types, Slide-GoTags detected TCR–neoantigen interactions through spatial proximity and identified an enrichment of interferon-driven immunogenicity niches in immunologically ‘hot’ tumors compared to ‘cold’ tumors.

insights.claim: The interferon signal is operationalised as the MP17 interferon and MHC II module score, which was compared across tumor regions and across four ccRCC sections and used to define immunogenicity-rich versus immunogenicity-poor regions.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A named, reusable module score is the portable part of the finding — other groups can apply MP17 to existing spatial datasets without the new assay.

insights.claim: Regions of high T cell density, high B cell density and MP17-expressing tumor cells overlap near tertiary lymphoid structure–like areas, identifying immune–tumor interaction niches that combine B cell help with interferon-high tumor cells.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Links the spatial niche concept back to TLS, already a leading response biomarker in RCC — convergent evidence strengthens the biomarker thesis.

insights.claim: In the same mouse tumor, Slide-GoTags detected 6 unique TRA and 15 unique TRB clonotypes versus only 2 TRA and 3 TRB detected by the 10x Genomics Chromium single-cell V(D)J kit, while both platforms consistently recovered the shared OT-I clones.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A roughly 3–5x clonotype-detection advantage over the market-standard 10x V(D)J kit is the commercially relevant number if this method is ever productised.

insights.claim: Slide-GoTags was also benchmarked head-to-head against Slide-TCR-seq on human ccRCC sections for the proportion of T cells with detected TCRα and TCRβ CDR3 sequences, with significance assessed by two-sided Fisher's exact tests and Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Direct comparison against the closest academic competitor is the evidence a buyer or licensee would demand before switching workflows.

insights.claim: Detection rates for TRA, TRB and SIINFEKL transcripts were compared across two independent Slide-GoTags replicates from separate tissue sections, addressing the reproducibility question that usually dogs low-input spatial assays.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Cross-section replication is the minimum bar for an assay heading toward regulated clinical use.

themes.theme: T cell exhaustion and avidity readouts

insights.claim: T cells carrying NSUN5 p.Q18K neoantigen-specific TCRs and other tumor-specific TCRs showed significantly higher exhaustion module scores than unrelated clonotypes (P = 1.3 × 10⁻⁶ and P = 9.73 × 10⁻¹³ respectively), meaning the very T cells that found their antigen are the most exhausted.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Antigen engagement drives exhaustion in situ — an argument that neoantigen therapies need exhaustion-reversal partners to convert engagement into killing.

insights.claim: Cytotoxicity module scores in NSUN5-TCR-expressing T cells differed significantly when stratified by TCR avidity (P = 0.004), tying a measurable receptor property to functional state inside the tissue.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Avidity-graded function supports screening TCR candidates on avidity for engineered T cell therapies rather than on specificity alone.

insights.claim: Exhaustion scores also differed significantly between spatial regions of the same tumor section (P = 0.016), indicating T cell state is regionally heterogeneous within a single specimen.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Intratumoral regional variation means single-biopsy immune profiling can misclassify a patient — an argument for spatial over bulk assays.

insights.claim: Progenitor-exhausted and terminally exhausted CD8+ T cell subsets were analysed separately for spatially co-occurring receptor–ligand interactions per patient, treating exhaustion as a trajectory with distinct spatial neighbourhoods rather than a single state.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Progenitor-exhausted cells are the population checkpoint inhibitors act on — locating their niche identifies where a drug has to reach.

insights.claim: Four authors including senior author Catherine J. Wu are listed as inventors on a patent application related to Slide-GoTags, so the method is encumbered IP rather than freely licensable technique.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Patent-pending status means any commercial spatial-genomics vendor wanting this capability has to negotiate with Dana-Farber rather than copy it.
insights.quote: A.N., J.Y.G., A. Sud and C.J.W. are listed as inventors on a patent application related to the work.

insights.claim: Co-senior author Fei Chen is an academic founder of Curio Bioscience and Doppler Bioscience and a scientific advisor to Amber Bio, placing the Slide-seq/Slide-tags lineage behind this method inside an existing commercial cluster.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Curio Bioscience already commercialises Slide-seq-derived chemistry — the most likely route to market for Slide-GoTags runs through it.

insights.claim: Catherine J. Wu holds equity in BioNTech and Nir Hacohen holds patents licensed to BioNTech, linking the neoantigen-mapping platform's senior authors directly to the leading personalised neoantigen vaccine developer.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: BioNTech is the named commercial channel with the strongest incentive to adopt spatial neoantigen readouts in its vaccine trials.

insights.claim: The work is heavily funded by kidney-cancer-specific sources — an NIH NCI grant (CA276865), the Mark Foundation Endeavor Award, the Dana-Farber/Harvard Cancer Center Kidney SPORE and Department of Defense Kidney Cancer Research Program awards — which explains why ccRCC is the lead human indication.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Funding gravity predicts where the first clinical application lands: renal cell carcinoma immunotherapy trials, not the broader pan-cancer market.

insights.claim: All four Slide-GoTags datasets were deposited to the Broad Institute Single Cell Portal (accessions SCP3655, SCP3657, SCP3660 and SCP3667) and processing code released on GitHub, so the analytical layer is reproducible even though the wet-lab method is patent-pending.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Open data plus closed IP is the standard academic-commercialisation posture — competitors can benchmark against the data but not replicate the chemistry freely.

insights.claim: The paper was received 12 December 2025, accepted 26 May 2026 and published 22 July 2026, a roughly five-and-a-half month review cycle for a method paper in Nature Biotechnology.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Dates the priority claim and bounds when competing groups could have seen the method in preprint or review.
